title: Ukrainian MoD: Russian Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,373,620 — +1,350 Eliminated in 24 Hours — Day 1,564
detail: On June 7, 2026 — Day 1,564 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukraine's Ministry of Defence published updated cumulative Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022. According to the Ukrainian General Staff, Russia has now sustained approximately 1,373,620 total personnel losses (killed, wounded, and missing), with approximately 1,350 personnel eliminated in the preceding 24-hour period. Equipment losses claimed by the Ukrainian MoD as of June 7: tanks — 11,989 (+6 daily); armored fighting vehicles — 24,700 (+4); artillery systems — 43,479 (+82); MLRS — 1,844 (+7); air defense assets — 1,407 (+2); aircraft — 436; helicopters — 353; UAVs — 334,063 (+2,245); cruise missiles — 4,733; warships/boats — 33; submarines — 2; unmanned ground vehicles — 1,595 (+10); vehicles and fuel tanks — 104,051 (+393); special equipment — 4,257 (+4). These figures are Ukrainian government estimates and cannot be independently verified; Russia has never released official casualty figures. The daily rate of ~1,350 reflects continued high-intensity fighting across the Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, Lyman, and Slovyansk sectors as Russia continues its attritional offensive pressure in eastern Ukraine.

title: Frontline: Russia Advances in Pokrovsk and Slovyansk Directions; Ukraine Holds Kostiantynivka — Day 1,564
detail: On June 7, 2026 — Day 1,564 of Russia's full-scale invasion — the frontline situation remained intense across all major sectors, with ISW confirming recent Russian advances in the Pokrovsk and Slovyansk directions and Ukrainian counter-advances in the Kostiantynivka direction. The Pokrovsk sector continues to be the most heavily contested area: Russia has mounted relentless pressure on this critical logistics hub throughout 2025-2026, and the town sits at the intersection of several supply routes for Ukrainian forces in central Donetsk Oblast. In the Slovyansk direction, geolocated footage indicated Russian forces pushing south and west toward the Siversky Donets River corridor. In the Kharkiv Oblast front, Russia continued pressing in the Sumy and Kharkiv border areas seeking to push ~20 km deep to establish a buffer zone — a stated Russian strategic objective that would require significant additional force commitment from Ukraine's already stretched northern flank. In Kostiantynivka, Ukrainian forces recently regained ground, reversing some Russian gains from late May 2026. Fighting also continued in the Kupiansk and Lyman directions with no confirmed territorial changes. The day's pattern reflected Russia's standard operational approach in summer 2026: sustained attritional pressure at multiple points along the 1,000+ km frontline, eroding Ukrainian defensive depth through sheer weight of artillery and infantry attacks even without dramatic single-day breakthroughs.
